findings.title: Guide misstates provider-failure 502 body
findings.problem: provisioning-api.md:71 says a failed provider sync in commit 2 'is 502 with the same message' ('partly applied; send the same request again'). A provider failure while creating the group actually reaches the caller as create_project_budget_group's own 502, 'Failed to sync project budget with enforcement provider': _create_group re-raises every non-409 error (provisioning_budget_service.py:466-467), and _commit_budget_after_project re-raises every non-4xx error (:416-417). Only the unsynced-category path (:447-449) uses PARTLY_APPLIED_MESSAGE, and test_provider_502_passes_through_and_resend_creates pins the pass-through. Spec Design 6 says LiteLLM's 502 is kept.
findings.impact: Future provisioning endpoints copy the pattern guide, and it states an error body the code does not produce. A client or endpoint author who keys on the 502 message gets group-create provider failures wrong, so the 'pattern is documented' criterion delivers an inaccurate rule.
findings.recommendation: Follow spec Design 6 ('LiteLLM's 502 is kept'): reword provisioning-api.md:71 so a provider failure during the group write passes the provider's own 502 through, and only a category left unsynced after commit 2 answers 502 'partly applied; send the same request again'.
findings.check_notes: provisioning-api.md:71 now says the provider's own 502 passes through and only an unsynced category is 502 partly applied; matches _commit_budget_after_project:420-426.

fix.change: provisioning-api.md commit-2 row: provider's own 502 passes through; unsynced category is 502 partly applied; 4xx or unexpected error is 500

findings.title: Input normalized before authorization decisions
findings.problem: security-patterns.md (Untrusted Input Handling) says to avoid stripping or silent coercion before a security decision. ProvisioningProjectName (strip_whitespace, to_lower) and NormalizedEmail (strip + lower) coerce the project_name path value, cost_center and admin_emails before _check_project decides whether manage-projects is required and whether the project is personal, and before the emails resolve to users who are made project admins. Spec Design 1 and the new provisioning-api.md:42 prescribe this normalization (carried over from the deleted servicenow model), so the spec and the security guide conflict.
findings.impact: Authorization and admin-grant decisions run on a value the caller did not send, and the new guide codifies the opposite of the security standard for every future provisioning endpoint. The security standards row stays partial until this is settled.
findings.recommendation: Decide which rule wins: either reject non-canonical names and emails with 422 (a lowercase pattern with no surrounding whitespace) instead of coercing them, or record an explicit, reasoned exception for identifier case-folding in security-patterns.md and align provisioning-api.md:42 with it.
findings.check_notes: Mapped decision (a) with hitl rationale: no coercion. Also implemented: ProvisioningProjectName is 3-100 only, admin_emails is list[EmailStr]; guide:42 and spec Design 1 aligned.

fix.change: ProvisioningProjectName keeps only 3-100 (no strip/lower); admin_emails is plain list[EmailStr]; assign_admins promotes a user once when two spellings resolve to it; path/model/guide/spec wording and OpenAPI baseline updated

decision.outcome: (a) Drop the coercion: project name, cost center and admin emails are used exactly as sent; no custom trimming or lowercasing; names keep the existing 3-100 rule (422); admin emails are plain EmailStr with no custom normalizer, as for member_email in EPMCDME-16904. provisioning-api.md:42 and the spec are aligned.
decision.rationale: security-patterns.md forbids coercing input before a security decision; the user chose the security standard over the spec's carried-over normalization at the review escalation (hitl).

findings.title: Cancel route OpenAPI docs misstate its contract
findings.problem: _CANCEL_RESPONSES includes _PARTLY_APPLIED_RESPONSES, so DELETE documents a 502 'The budget provider sync failed; the call was partly applied'. cancel_budget is a single commit, never raises PARTLY_APPLIED_MESSAGE, and has no provider-failure 502 path, because a failed provider deletion is swallowed (DF-004). _CANCEL_DESCRIPTION also leaves out the resend-after-5xx sentence that provisioning-api.md requires of every write route ('Every write route's description says so'). The shared 422 text mentions a body that DELETE does not take.
findings.impact: External provisioning clients build their retry logic from this OpenAPI contract. The DELETE contract advertises an outcome it cannot produce and leaves out the one rule the guide says every write route states.
findings.recommendation: Give DELETE its own 422 text (project name or X-Change-Reference header, no body), drop the 502 'budget provider sync failed' entry from _CANCEL_RESPONSES, word its 500 entry for cancel, and add the 'a 4xx means nothing changed; after a 5xx send the same request again' sentence to _CANCEL_DESCRIPTION. If DELETE is later made to surface provider-deletion failure (DF-004), document that 502 deliberately.
findings.check_notes: _CANCEL_RESPONSES (budgets.py:123-138) has a no-body 422, a cancel-specific 500 and no 502; _CANCEL_DESCRIPTION:89-90 states the 4xx/resend rule.

fix.change: DELETE gets its own 422 (no body) and 500 texts, no 502, and the 4xx/resend sentence in its description

findings.title: Write-route 403/400 docs omit conditions
findings.problem: provisioning-api.md requires the route's 403 description to name every condition that can produce it. The _WRITE_RESPONSES 403 text leaves out the cost-centers-disabled 403 from CostCenterService.ensure_feature_enabled, reached through check_project_prerequisites -> _check_cost_center. The 400 text, 'The amounts do not make a valid budget.', leaves out the 400s for an invalid new project name (ProjectService.validate_shared_project_name) and an invalid cost center name (CostCenterService.validate_name).
findings.impact: A provisioning client that receives these 403 or 400 answers cannot map them to the published contract, and the change breaks a rule that it documents itself.
findings.recommendation: Add the cost-centers-disabled case to the 403 description (the call would create or link a cost center while the feature is off), and add the invalid new project name and invalid cost center name cases to the 400 description.
findings.check_notes: _WRITE_RESPONSES 400 (budgets.py:96-102) names invalid new project and cost center names; 403 (:103-111) names cost centers disabled.

fix.change: Write-route 403 adds cost-centers-disabled; 400 adds invalid new project name and invalid cost center name; OpenAPI baseline regenerated

findings.title: Unchanged re-save no longer repairs member pushes
findings.problem: _effective_project_budget_values now sets amounts_changed only when a stored max, soft limit or duration differs or the budget's own sync_status is not ok, so re-saving unchanged amounts skips _resync_member_allocations. Before this change, any supplied amount re-ran the member resync. A failed member push is swallowed with no failure marker: _resync_member_allocation logs a warning and returns None (:1179-1187). The runtime path does not repair it either, because ensure_project_member_runtime_ready returns early when the member's provider ref and budget id are current (project_member_runtime_sync.py:128-143). Every new test mocks _resync_member_allocations, so no test models a failed member push followed by an unchanged re-save. The edge-case lens's deletion row also covers provider-key re-pushes; that part is mandated by AC20 and is not a defect.
findings.impact: After one failed member push, the member keeps a stale provider limit. Nothing repairs it: not the admin REST PUT (project_budget_router.py:313), not a group update, not a provisioning resend. The regression ships unnoticed because no test covers it.
findings.recommendation: Make a failed member push count as a failed sync that the next update retries (for example, record a failure marker on the allocation or budget and include it in amounts_changed). Add the lifecycle test the lens describes: stored budget ok, a member allocation whose previous provider push raised, update_project_budget called with the stored values, assert the allocation is synced again.
findings.check_notes: _resync_member_allocation:1196-1201 marks a failed push FAILED; update_project_budget:1348 resyncs when any allocation is FAILED; _sync_member_allocation:540-552 clears it on success.

fix.change: _resync_member_allocation marks a failed member push FAILED on the allocation; update_project_budget re-syncs when any allocation is FAILED

findings.title: Resync rule re-syncs noop and pending budgets
findings.problem: Spec Design 6 requires pbs to sync a category only when its effective max, soft limit or duration changed, or its last sync failed. _effective_project_budget_values sets amounts_changed whenever last_sync_status != SyncStatus.OK, so NOOP and PENDING also trigger a provider sync and _resync_member_allocations on every unchanged update (reported by the blind, edge-case and acceptance lenses). provisioning_budget_service._SYNCED_STATUSES = {OK, NOOP} treats NOOP as synced, so the two modules disagree on what synced means.
findings.impact: A required spec behavior is only partly met (the acceptance row is partial). Every unchanged update of a noop or pending budget, including the admin REST PUT, re-runs the provider sync and the member reallocation, and the provisioning 502 check and the pbs resync rule use different definitions of synced.
findings.recommendation: Retry only when the last sync failed, as the spec says (`or last_sync_status == SyncStatus.FAILED`), and keep NOOP counted as synced, as provisioning_budget_service._SYNCED_STATUSES does. If PENDING must also retry, define one shared set of synced statuses for both modules and record that rule in the spec. Keep the CR-005 failure marker inside the same rule.
findings.check_notes: Shared SYNCED_STATUSES {ok,noop} (budget_enums.py) drives pbs amounts_changed (:729) and the provisioning unsynced check (:452); noop no longer resyncs; spec Design 6 records the pending retry.

fix.change: Shared SYNCED_STATUSES={ok,noop} in budget_enums used by pbs resync rule and provisioning 502 check; noop no longer re-syncs, pending still does; spec Design 6 line updated

findings.title: cat_spec typed as Any in new method
findings.problem: code-quality.md (Types And Imports) requires spelling out the accepted union for a duck-typed parameter. The new _check_category_plan declares cat_spec: Any, although it receives the CategoryBudgetSpec | CategoryBudgetSpecUpdate values of ProjectBudgetGroupCreateRequest | ProjectBudgetGroupUpdateRequest.
findings.impact: New code does not meet the documented typing standard (the code-quality standards row is partial), and type checking cannot catch misuse of pct or soft_budget on the spec.
findings.check_notes: _check_category_plan cat_spec is CategoryBudgetSpec | CategoryBudgetSpecUpdate via TYPE_CHECKING imports; from __future__ import annotations present; Any still used elsewhere.

findings.title: Client 4xx rejections logged at ERROR
findings.problem: _failure_logged logs every exception with logger.error, including routine 400/403/404/409 caller rejections such as cancelling a project that does not exist. logging-patterns.md:34 lists 'Error logs for expected validation failures' as an anti-pattern and says to use a warning or a structured client error instead.
findings.impact: Caller mistakes from external provisioning clients show up at ERROR and feed error-level alerting, burying real 5xx causes.
findings.recommendation: Log ExtendedHTTPException with 400 <= code < 500 at warning, and keep error for 5xx and unexpected exceptions.
findings.check_notes: _failure_logged (provisioning_budget_service.py:216-224) logs a 4xx ExtendedHTTPException at warning and everything else at error.

fix.change: _failure_logged logs 4xx ExtendedHTTPException at warning, 5xx and unexpected errors at error

findings.title: manage-projects checked only on check-phase snapshot
findings.problem: _check_project requires manage-projects only when find_project returned None during the check phase. Commit 1 (_commit_project_once -> ProvisioningService.resolve_project) reads the project again and creates it when it is missing, without checking the permission again. The project delete path hard-deletes the row (ProjectService -> application_repository.delete_by_name, project_service.py:724), so a project deleted between the two phases is recreated by a client that holds only manage-budgets.
findings.impact: In that window, a client without manage-projects creates a project, which is exactly what the permission is meant to stop (D12). The race needs a concurrent admin delete of a resource-free project, so it cannot be triggered at will.
findings.recommendation: In _commit_project_once, before session.commit(), require manage-projects when resolve_project created the project but the check phase did not require it. Raise 403 there: commit 1 has not committed yet, so the 4xx still means nothing changed. Alternatively, pass the check phase's project presence into resolve_project and refuse to create.
findings.check_notes: _commit_project_once:381-383 calls require_permission(MANAGE_PROJECTS) when resolve_project created the project, before session.commit(), so the 403 leaves nothing committed.

fix.change: _commit_project_once requires manage-projects before commit when resolve_project created the project

findings.title: Non-HTTP errors after commit 1 skip partly-applied
findings.problem: _commit_budget_after_project converts only ExtendedHTTPException 4xx errors. Three other kinds escape as a generic 500, without _log_partly_applied: an IntegrityError that _create_group re-raises when no group survives the conflict, a pydantic ValidationError from _create_request/_update_request during re-planning, and any provider or DB exception. The _failure_logged line carries no project= field (reported by the blind and edge-case lenses).
findings.impact: After commit 1 has stored the project, the 500 body lacks the documented partly-applied message, and the cause is logged without the project. That contradicts provisioning-api.md: 'The cause of a 5xx is logged with client, change_reference and the project'.
findings.recommendation: In _commit_budget_after_project, also catch Exception: call _log_partly_applied(call, project_name, _failure_reason(e)) and raise ExtendedHTTPException(code=500, message=PARTLY_APPLIED_MESSAGE) from e. Add project= to the _failure_logged line.
findings.check_notes: _commit_budget_after_project:420-426 catches Exception; only HTTP 5xx passes through, the rest is logged as partly applied and raised as 500; the _failure_logged line carries project=.

fix.change: _commit_budget_after_project turns any non-5xx-HTTP error into 500 partly applied with _log_partly_applied; failure log carries project=

findings.title: Deleted cost-center link hides named cost center
findings.problem: A project linked to a soft-deleted cost center keeps cost_center_id set, so check_project_prerequisites skips the named cost center and resolve_project never links it, while _active_cost_center_name reports cost_center as null (pinned by test_deleted_link_is_reported_as_no_cost_center). The caller sees 'not linked' and resends with a cost center, but the link never changes (reported by the blind and edge-case lenses).
findings.impact: Billing linkage silently stays on a deleted cost center while the response claims there is no link, and the client cannot fix it by resending. The spec says an existing link never changes, but it does not say whether a link to a deleted cost center counts.
findings.recommendation: Decide the intended behavior. Either treat a link to a deleted cost center as unlinked and link the named one, reject the call with 409 naming the deleted linked cost center, or report the deleted link's name instead of null. Then update the spec and the pinning test.
findings.check_notes: Mapped decision (a) with hitl rationale. Also implemented: set_cost_center_if_unset replaces a deleted link; check_project_prerequisites:103-106 and resolve_project:130-139 treat it as none.

fix.change: A link to a deleted cost center counts as none: set_cost_center_if_unset also replaces it (deleted-ids subquery), check_project_prerequisites checks and resolve_project links the named one; descriptions and spec updated

decision.outcome: (a) A link to a deleted cost center counts as no link, so the named cost center is checked and linked; the pinning test and the spec are updated.
decision.rationale: Matches the cost_center: null the response already reports, and lets a client repair the link by resending; decided by the user at the review escalation (hitl).

findings.title: Lost link race reports created cost center
findings.problem: When a concurrent call links another cost center first, link_cost_center_in_session returns the stored link (because of the set_cost_center_if_unset IS NULL guard). created_cost_center stays True from CostCenterService.get_or_create, so the response reports created_cost_center true next to a different cost_center, and the newly created cost center is committed unlinked.
findings.impact: Under concurrent provisioning calls, the response misreports what was created and an orphan cost center is committed.
findings.recommendation: After link_cost_center_in_session, set created_cost_center = created_cost_center and cost_center_id == named.id, so that a lost race never reports a cost center as created next to a different linked one.
findings.check_notes: resolve_project:145 reports created_cost_center only when the stored link is the named cost center.

fix.change: resolve_project reports created_cost_center only when the named cost center is the one linked

deferred.preexisting: The deleted servicenow model had the same ge=0, allow_inf_nan=False amount rule; the spec keeps today's amount rules.

deferred.preexisting: The pbs delete path predates this change; the deleted servicenow cancel called delete_project_budget_group the same way.

deferred.title: pct search duplicates the budget amount formula
deferred.problem: _exact_pct derives amounts through its own _derived_amount copy instead of ProjectBudgetService._category_amount (identical today), and no test ties the two together.
deferred.preexisting: _derived_amount was copied verbatim from the deleted servicenow_integration_service; the two formulas match today.

deferred.title: Concurrent cancels can answer 404
deferred.problem: _delete_group reads the active group without a row lock, so when two concurrent DELETEs both find it, the loser's delete_project_budget_group raises 404.
deferred.preexisting: The deleted servicenow cancel read the group the same way, unlocked through get_active_by_project.
